readout_other: Longa neurological score; open field, rotarod and novel object recognition tests; 9.4 T MRI infarct and edema volume; TTC staining; blood counts, LDL-C, homocysteine, glucose; qPCR and Western blot (iNOS, eNOS, PECAM1, VEGF-A, nNOS, BDNF); CD31 immunofluorescence
direction_notes: Neural activity was not measured. Daily LITUS for 14 days after MCAO improved body weight, Longa scores, motor and cognitive behaviour and upregulated angiogenic and neurotrophic markers versus untreated MCAO rats, in both moderate (ML) and HITUS-aggravated (MHL) injury.

exposures.label: LITUS after MCAO (ML) and after MCAO plus HITUS injury (MHL groups)

device.manufacturer: Green Valley Brain Medical Technology Co., Ltd.
device.model: GVBT-1-A001 single-channel stimulator with 20 mm planar transducer

timing.protocol_description: Pulses of 200 us with a duty cycle of 20 %, delivered in cycles repeated every 2 s, each stimulation period lasting 1 s; 20 min daily for 14 consecutive days starting 24 h (ML) or 48 h after HITUS (MHL) after MCAO. A separate high-intensity injury exposure (1 MHz, 20 min, Isppa 27.5 W/cm2, Ispta 3300 mW/cm2) was given to MHL rats 24 h after MCAO to aggravate damage.

flags.reason: 20 % duty cycle with 200 us pulses implies a PRF the paper does not state; PRF left not_reported and nothing computed.
0.93 MPa is called the 'local peak-to-peak acoustic pressure' measured; domain (water or skull) not stated, so placed in unspecified_domain. Isppa 7.70 W/cm2 and Ispta 770 mW/cm2 likewise.
Effective Ispta 462 mW/cm2 at the target after a stated 40 % attenuation through rat skull by hydrophone measurement.
Group sizes of the two LITUS-treated groups (MHL and ML, 15 each); 60 rats in total across four groups, two of them not sonicated with LITUS. Figures report n = 12 or fewer per group.
Target not named beyond the ipsilateral hemisphere and the infarcted cortex; planar 20 mm transducer with 8 mm focal depth.
Each stimulation period lasts 1 s, repeated every 2 s.
Isoflurane is described for MCAO surgery; anaesthesia during LITUS is not stated.
Second exposure (HITUS injury) at the same 1 MHz and target is described in protocol_description rather than as a separate exposure; its stated AMP of 31 Pa is not a pressure that can be used.
